v.why: Replacing a removed direct edge with a 3x3 conv adds a useful path, whereas replacing any other op gives a smaller gain or a loss.
Adding a skip where the edge was none restores a direct input-to-output path, while replacing a conv with skip tends to hurt.
Replacing none on the first edge activates the whole node-1 branch, so the gain is much larger than when upgrading an existing op.
Replacing none on the last edge into the output reconnects node 2's path, a larger gain than swapping one op for another.
Replacing none with a conv on 0->2 creates a new feature path, a larger gain than replacing another op.
Removing a conv from the direct edge costs much more accuracy than removing a pool or skip.
Deleting a conv on the first edge cuts off node 1's learned features, which hurts more than deleting a weak op.
With 0->2 removed, node 2 gets input only via node 1, so a conv on 2->3 is worth less.
With 0->1 removed, node 1 has no input, so a conv on 1->3 is useless.
With 0->1 removed, node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on 1->2 adds nothing.
